records.place: O Bolo, Val do Bibei, Valdeorras, Galicia

wine.name: As Sortes Val do Bibei
wine.grapes: Godello alone, from old vines planted by local growers in the late 1970s and early 1980s.
wine.sites: Six small sortes, by the house's account, on the north face of the Bibei valley at Santa Cruz do Bolo, above 680 metres on sandy, decomposed granite, their Godello about forty years old on average.
wine.making: By the house's own page the must ferments in 500 litre oak barrels and the wine then ages about eight months in them, worked on its lees, before bottling.
wine.glass: Red apple, pear skin and lemon with a faintly balsamic note over wet granite; creamy from the lees yet taut, with saline acidity and a long, stony finish.
wine.ageing: Taut in youth, it can be opened from a year or two after the vintage, and it keeps and gains depth for a decade and often longer.
wine.serve: 10 to 13 degrees Celsius, not too cold, so the texture shows; no need to decant; a wide white wine glass such as a Burgundy glass.

label.means: The sortes: small plots once shared out among heirs by drawing lots, as the Galician word recalls.
The valley of the Bibei, a tributary of the Sil, where the house's vines grow around O Bolo.
The Godello country of the Sil valley in eastern Ourense, Galicia's second oldest denomination by its own account.
The white grape of Valdeorras, almost lost by the early 1970s and saved by a replanting plan begun in 1974.

records.table: As Sortes is the Godello of Rafael Palacios, from old plots high in the Bibei valley of Valdeorras, fermented and aged in 500 litre oak barrels on its lees. Creamy yet taut, with pear, red apple and a stony, saline finish, it wants serving not too cold.
records.story: Godello was close to vanishing from Valdeorras by the early 1970s, when the replanting plan known as ReViVal, begun in 1974 and honoured by the denomination as the grape's rescue, set out to gather its last old vines and propagate them. Thirty years later a younger member of the Palacios family, whose bodega in Rioja and whose houses in Priorat and Bierzo carry the name further, struck out on his own after years in the family firm. In 2004 he set up this house at O Bolo in the Bibei valley, buying old Godello vineyards from elderly local growers. Between 2004 and 2007 he gathered six small sortes, plots planted by local growers in the late 1970s and early 1980s; the word recalls the custom of dividing land among heirs by drawing lots. Those sortes give As Sortes, fermented and aged in 500 litre barrels, while the simpler Louro and the single plot wines were set beside it. For a sommelier As Sortes is the wine that shows what Godello can be: a white of texture and stone that rewards a cellar, and much of the reason Valdeorras is the denomination named for the grape.

others.name: Louro
others.note: The house's simpler Godello, with a little Treixadura, fermented in large French oak foudres and kept a few months on its fine lees.

others.name: Sorte O Soro
others.note: A single sorte of Godello planted on terraces in 1978, fermented and aged in 500 litre barrels like As Sortes, by the house's page.

others.name: Sorte Antiga
others.note: The house's oldest plot, Godello planted in 1920 as bush vines on their own roots, fermented on its skins in open oak vats.

traps: Godello is neither Verdejo nor Albariño, and As Sortes is a white of inland Ourense, not of the coast of Rías Baixas.
Rafael Palacios in Valdeorras is a house of its own: the family's houses in Rioja, Priorat and Bierzo are separate producers with separate wines.
Val do Bibei on the label is the valley of the Bibei inside Valdeorras; Dominio do Bibei, downstream at Manzaneda, is a Ribeira Sacra house.

cards.front: Rafael Palacios: what are the sortes behind As Sortes?
cards.back: Small old plots of Godello in the Bibei valley, gathered between 2004 and 2007; the word recalls land shared out among heirs by lot.

cards.front: What began in Valdeorras in 1974 that later made As Sortes possible?
cards.back: The ReViVal plan, which gathered and propagated the last old Godello vines when the grape was close to lost.

questions.q: A guest asks how Rafael Palacios makes As Sortes. Which cellar matches the house's own account?
opts: Fermented and aged in 500 litre oak barrels
Fermented in steel and bottled within weeks
Aged under a veil of flor in a solera
Fermented on its skins in clay jars
questions.exp: The house's page gives fermentation in 500 litre barrels and about eight months in barrel on the lees; steel and quick bottling is the way of a simpler, fresher Godello.

questions.q: In 2004 a member of the Palacios family of Rioja set up a house at O Bolo in Valdeorras. What did it buy first?
opts: Old Godello vines from local growers
A monastery cellar beside the Sil
A co-operative's winery at O Barco
Young Albariño vines near the coast
questions.exp: By the house's own history it began by buying old Godello vines from aged growers of the Bibei valley; Albariño is the grape of the coast, not of inland Valdeorras.

report: Searches for this record: 6 of the group's share of 35 (two on the house's own domain), beside one shared with A Tapada on the DO Valdeorras's own domain; the group used 32 searches of its 35 in all and one fetch, refused.

The library's style line says fermented and aged in large wood; the house's own As Sortes page gives 500 litre barrels and about eight months, and the large French oak foudres of 35 hectolitres belong to Louro, so the record follows the house and the library line reads loosely rather than wrongly.

The six sortes, their planting in the late 1970s and early 1980s, Santa Cruz do Bolo, the height above 680 metres and their being the oldest vineyards the house owns are on the house's own pages; one merchant counts seven plots for the 2014 vintage, so the record says six by the house's account.

The meaning of sorte, a plot shared out among heirs by lot, rests on Liberty Wines and Wine.com's listing; the years in the family's Rioja firm rest on two merchants' profiles (Vinissimus and Grand Cru Wijnen), and Plácet, the white the founder made there, is left out for want of a second dated source.

Not borne out and left out: 2004 as the first vintage of As Sortes, and the house's own forecast of twenty to twenty five years in bottle (a merchant's blog); the ageing line follows the merchants' drinking windows.

The ReViVal plan of 1974, Godello's near loss and the DO's claim to be Galicia's second oldest are on the DO Valdeorras's own pages, as the region record says; the DO's eightieth year in 2025 points to 1945 for its council, which the record does not state because no page read gave the year itself.

Living names met, none in the fragment's prose: the house's founder (the house keeps his name, he is never named as a person) and his brother of the Priorat house; the DO pages name the ReViVal's promoter and an oenologist, both of unknown status and both left out.
Of the label, the record prints only As Sortes, Val do Bibei, Valdeorras and Godello, each on the merchants' listings of the bottle.

changed: wine.sites: they are the oldest of the house's own vineyards cut (Sorte Antiga of 1920 is), the northern side now the north face, sandy granite and Godello of about forty years by the house's page (house pages, Vinos con Carácter, Songbird, Sobre Lías).
wine.ageing: often left about five years to open now opened from a year or two after the vintage, keeping a decade and often longer (Decanter, Sokolin, Grand Cru Wijnen, Lay Wheeler).
others: O Soro now a sorte planted on terraces in 1978 in 500 litre barrels, Sorte Antiga the house's oldest plot, on its own roots, fermented on its skins (the house's pages and two merchants).
traps[2]: Dominio do Bibei upstream now downstream at Manzaneda (Turismo de Galicia, the rivers of Galicia).
questions[1]: the key shortened to Old Godello vines from local growers; sources: Polaner and Sobre Lías for Liberty and Berry Bros.
open: The ReViVal's first year: 1974 by the Xunta's DOG of 2024 and the DO's fiftieth year in 2024, 1975 on another DO page; the record keeps 1974.

The library's large wood for As Sortes: true of the first vintages (the 2005 in 3,000 litre foudres by Verema's vertical), while the house's page gives 500 litre barrels; the vintage of the change was not found.
Louro's little Treixadura rests on the library in what the refuter read; Polaner gives Louro do Bolo from younger vines in 35 hectolitre foudres for four months on fine lees.
The years in the family's Rioja firm rest on the author's two merchants and Polaner's leaving of the Rioja estate in 2004; Plácet stays out.

wine.name: Guitián Godello Sobre Lías
wine.grapes: Godello alone, from the family's own estate.
wine.sites: The family estate of A Tapada at Rubiá, in the Sil valley of Valdeorras, replanted with Godello alone from 1985 when the grape was nearly forgotten.
wine.making: Fermented in stainless steel at a controlled temperature, then kept for some four to six months on its fine lees in tank, stirred weekly, with no oak at any stage, before it is bottled young. The lees, rather than wood, give it its creamy texture.
wine.glass: A stony nose of ripe white fruit, fresh butter and nuts, with a hint of sunflower seed; dry and creamy on the palate from the lees, with firm acidity and a long, clean finish.
wine.ageing: Made to drink young, from its release to about three years after the vintage, while its freshness and creamy texture hold together.
wine.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; no need to decant; a white wine glass of middling size.

label.means: The family name of the brothers who replanted A Tapada, used as the brand of all the house's wines.
On the lees: kept for months on its fine lees in tank after fermentation, without oak.
The denomination of the Sil, Xares and Bibei valleys in eastern Ourense, beside Bierzo, where Godello is at home.

records.table: Guitián Sobre Lías is the Godello of Bodegas A Tapada, from the family estate at Rubiá in Valdeorras, made in steel and kept for months on its fine lees with no oak. Dry, creamy and firm, it is the fresh face of the grape, for fish and shellfish.
records.story: Godello had almost vanished from Valdeorras by the 1970s, and the ReViVal replanting plan of 1974 had only begun to gather and propagate its last old vines. A decade on, the Guitián family staked its estate on the grape. In 1985 the brothers of the family, led by one of them, replanted their estate of A Tapada at Rubiá, in the Sil valley, with Godello alone, at a time when it was all but forgotten, and the wines took the family's name. They worked from the start with consulting oenologists, and in the middle of the 1990s made a Godello fermented in barrel, by the house's account the first of its kind. About ten years after the founding the brother who had led the project was killed in a road accident; his brother and sister carried it on. The house kept two paths for the one grape: the barrel wine, and Sobre Lías, made in steel and rested on its fine lees with no wood. For a sommelier Guitián is one of the names of Godello's return: an estate replanted with the grape in 1985, years before Valdeorras was known abroad for it.

others.name: Guitián Godello Fermentado en Barrica
others.note: The barrel fermented Godello of the house, first made in the middle of the 1990s.

others.name: Guitián Godello Vendimia Tardía

traps: The label says Guitián, the family's name, while the house is Bodegas A Tapada, named for its estate at Rubiá: they are one producer, not two.
Sobre Lías means time on the lees in steel, not in barrel: the house's barrel fermented Godello is a separate wine.

cards.front: A Tapada: what does Sobre Lías on the Guitián label tell you?
cards.back: Kept some months on its fine lees in steel after fermentation, with no oak, for a creamy texture.

cards.front: When and how did the Guitián family remake its estate at Rubiá?
cards.back: In 1985, replanting A Tapada with Godello alone when the grape was nearly forgotten in Valdeorras.

Fermentation and a year in new French barrels
A long rest under flor in old casks
A blend with Albariño from the coast
questions.exp: Sobre Lías is fermented in steel and rests some four to six months on its fine lees with no wood; the barrel fermented Guitián is the house's other Godello.

Palomino
Mencía
Treixadura

report: Searches for this record: 4 of the group's share of 35, beside the one shared with Rafael Palacios on the DO Valdeorras's domain; the house's own site was found in no result, so every fact rests on two secondary sources or on the DO's own page.

The plan's note is answered by choosing Guitián Godello Sobre Lías: it holds the plan's words, its making is on two merchants' sheets (steel at a controlled temperature, four to six months on fine lees by Gourmet Hunters, six months by En Copa de Balón) and the region record's line, kept on its lees or fermented in barrel, covers it; the barrel wine is in others.
Founded is 1985 on Spanish Wine Lover, Vozpópuli and Enterwine, each telling the brothers' replanting of A Tapada with Godello alone.

The first barrel fermented Godello is the house's claim as Enterwine prints it (Guitián Fermentado en Barrica 1996), while Vozpópuli dates the first barrel wine to the 1995 vintage, so the record says the middle of the 1990s and hedges the first.

The brother who led the project died in a road accident in 1996 by Vozpópuli and about ten years after the founding by Spanish Wine Lover; his birth year was found nowhere, so he is described, not named.

Left out for want of a second source: the estate's soils (slate and granite terraces in one producer's description on a merchant's page), its height, the weekly stirring of the lees, a prize in Bordeaux for the first barrel wine, and a merchant's story that a Guitián tasted in 1999 drew the Rafael Palacios house to Godello.

Living names met, none in the fragment's prose: the sister and brother who carry the house on and its two consulting oenologists, as Spanish Wine Lover names them; the brothers are said as the family. Not in WINE_PRODUCERS; Godeval, the plan's alternative, was not needed and no swap is proposed.

changed: wine.making: the lees stirred weekly added (El Gusto por el Vino, Vinos Baco, Alforins, the house).
wine.label[2].means: from O Barco to A Rúa, which left out Rubiá, now the Sil, Xares and Bibei valleys beside Bierzo (the DO's page).
sources: the house's own Quiénes somos and El Gusto por el Vino for Gourmet Hunters and En Copa de Balón.
open: The first barrel fermented Godello: 1996 as the first in the world by the house's account in one result, 1995 by Vozpópuli, barrel trials in 1994 by another; the record tells the house's claim of the middle 1990s.
The first wine and the winery building: 1992 by two accounts for the first Guitián, 1995 or the early 1990s for the building; neither is stated in the record.
The brother's death: late 1996 by one account, about ten years after the founding by another; his dates were found nowhere, so he stays described.

wine.name: Algueira Pizarra
wine.grapes: Mencía, alone or very nearly so.
wine.sites: Terraces of slate on the steep, south facing slopes of Doade above the Sil, in the Amandi subzone, by the house's own sheet.
wine.making: Picked by hand on terraces too steep for machines, the Mencía is fermented and then aged in French oak, barrels and larger foudres, for twelve to eighteen months by vintage, before a rest in tank and bottling.
wine.glass: Violets, black cherry and sour cranberry over a clear smell of wet slate; medium bodied and fresh, with fine tannin and a long, stony finish.
wine.ageing: Drinks well from two or three years after the vintage and keeps for several years more, gaining savoury notes as the fruit softens.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius, a light chill rather than room warmth; decant a young bottle briefly to lift its perfume; a Burgundy glass.

label.means: Spanish for slate, the stone of the Doade terraces the vines grow on.
Galician for winery, as bodega is in Spanish.
The denomination of the Sil and Miño canyons, recognised by the Xunta de Galicia in 1995 and confirmed with its rules in 1996.

records.table: Algueira Pizarra is a Mencía from the slate terraces of Doade above the Sil, in Ribeira Sacra's Amandi subzone, made by a family that began rebuilding abandoned terraces there in 1979. Violets, black cherry and wet stone: pour it with a light chill.
records.story: The slopes of Doade, on the Lugo bank of the Sil, have carried vines for many centuries, by the house's account for at least fifteen, and the stone terraces that hold them were built by hand into the canyon wall. By the second half of the twentieth century many lay abandoned. In 1979 the family behind Algueira took on Carballo Cobo, then a run of half ruined terraces on a steep slope, and began to rebuild them, a work the house has kept up since, bringing back vines that were nearly lost. Ribeira Sacra, recognised as a denomination in 1995, was confirmed with its rules by an order of the Xunta de Galicia of 3 September 1996, with Amandi among its five subzones, and Algueira stands among the wineries of Amandi. Beside Mencía the house grows the old native reds of the canyon, Brancellao, Sousón, Caíño and Merenzao, and in time bottled some of them alone. Pizarra, named for the slate beneath the vines, is the house's Mencía aged in barrel. For a sommelier it is a clear lesson in what Amandi's south facing slate gives the grape: ripeness and perfume, held by a stony freshness, from vineyards that can only be worked by hand.

others.name: Carravel
others.note: A Mencía from chosen plots of Doade, each fermented apart and blended after long ageing in French oak, by the house's sheet.

others.name: Risco
others.note: The house's red of Merenzao alone, from gneiss and slate facing south west, by its sheet.

others.name: Serradelo
others.note: The house's red of Brancellao, from schist, slate and gneiss facing south, by its sheet.

traps: Pizarra is Spanish for slate, not a vineyard, a village or a grape: the wine is Mencía from the slate of Doade.
Merenzao, which Algueira also bottles, is a separate red grape from Mencía, paler and more perfumed.

cards.front: Algueira Pizarra carries Ribeira Sacra: when was that denomination authorised?
cards.back: Recognised in 1995 and confirmed, with its rules, by an order of the Xunta de Galicia of 3 September 1996; Amandi is one of its five subzones.

report: Searches for this record: 6 of the group's share of 35 (one on the house's own domain), beside one shared with Dominio do Bibei on the Consejo's domain; the group's one fetch, of an export agent's Pizarra page, was refused (the host does not resolve here) and never retried.

Founded is empty, as the plan's note asks: the sources give 1979 for the first vineyard (the house and two profiles), 1980 for the founder's arrival, 1996 for the winery building, 2000 for the first wines under the Algueira name and the early or late 1990s for the house; none agrees on a founding.

The plan's why calls Algueira one of the founding wineries of the DO of 1996; that rests on one producer profile (Wine Scholar Guild, read through search) and is left out, though the Consejo's guide of 2016 lists the house first among Amandi's wineries.

The grapes: Bodeboca gives Mencía alone for the 2010 and 2015 vintages and Liberty Wines a Mencía led blend with Brancellao and Caíño from Abeleda for a recent one, hence alone or very nearly so; the Carballocovo source of the Mencía rests on Liberty alone and is hedged.

The barrel: twelve months in French oak for the 2010 (Bodeboca), twelve in French barriques and foudres (Liberty), fourteen in barrel then tank for the 2017 (Bodeboca); whole bunches trodden by foot, cold maceration, the stems and native yeasts rest on Liberty's sheet alone and are left out.

Is Pizarra the flagship? No source calls it so; the house's own pages single out Carballocovo, its Homenaje (36 months in barrel for the 2013) and its native grape reds, while Pizarra is the barrel aged Mencía merchants list most widely, so the pick stands and no swap is proposed.
The tasting words come from Bodeboca's notes (violets, black cherry, sour cranberry, slate); the region record's Merenzao as the Trousseau of the Jura is not repeated here.
Living names met, none in the fragment's prose: the founder, his wife and their son, and the Bierzo winemaker said to have worked with the house (already in people.json).

changed: wine.sites: the importer's Carballocovo as Pizarra's vineyard cut (one account); slate and the south aspect by the house's sheet.
wine.making: twelve to fourteen months in French oak barrels now twelve to eighteen months in French barrels and foudres by vintage (the house, Vinos con Carácter, Xadigal, Dicomar).

wine.label[2], story, cards[1]: authorised on 3 September 1996 now recognised in 1995 and confirmed with its rules on 3 September 1996 (the DOG and the Xunta); Carballocovo spelt Carballo Cobo as two results quoting the house give it.
others: Algueira Mencía, found on no page, and Algueira Merenzao now the house's Carravel, Risco and Serradelo by its sheets.
questions: the wine explanation no longer names a vineyard, the story key shortened; sources: the house's Pizarra sheet, the DOG of 1996 and Vinos con Carácter.
open: The vineyard's spelling: Carballo Cobo in two results that quote the house; the author read Carballocovo on the house's Homenaje page, which the refuter could not read. The integrator may wish to see that page.
Pizarra's vineyard: Carballo Cobo by Liberty, Abeleda for part of a recent vintage by Liberty, a single vineyard of old vines by Antalva; not settled, so the record names none.
Founding: 1979 for the first vineyard, 1980 for the founder's arrival, 1996 for the building, 1998 for the brand, 2005 by Decanter; founded stays empty.
The founding member of the DO of 1996: one producer guide again (the same Wine Scholar Guild entry), so it stays out.
The fifteen centuries of vines at Doade: the house's account, Roman times by one importer; told as the house's.

wine.name: Lalama
wine.grapes: Mencía, the great majority, with small shares of Brancellao, Mouratón and Sousón and a little Garnacha, which some sheets name Garnacha Tintorera or Alicante Bouschet.
wine.sites: Steep terraces of the Bibei valley at the eastern edge of Ribeira Sacra, by the Valdeorras border, mostly on slate and schist with granite and some clay, from about 300 metres to 700 and higher by some accounts.
wine.making: Fermented with native yeasts in large open wooden vats, the wine is then raised in used barrels and larger oak vats or foudres for a year and more, up to about twenty months by vintage, before bottling.
wine.glass: Cherry, plum and pomegranate with violet and a little blood orange over graphite and wet stone; medium bodied and fresh, with fine grained tannin and the oak kept in the background.
wine.ageing: Firm in youth, it wants four or five years from the vintage to open and keeps for a decade and more in a strong year.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle an hour ahead to open its perfume; a Burgundy glass.

label.means: The estate of the Bibei, the river whose steep valley holds the house's terraces.
The denomination of the Sil and Miño canyons; Quiroga-Bibei is its eastern subzone, on the Bibei towards Valdeorras.

records.table: Lalama is the red of Dominio do Bibei, from the steep terraces of the Bibei valley at the eastern edge of Ribeira Sacra: mostly Mencía with a little of the valley's other red grapes, fermented with native yeasts and raised in used wood. Pour it lightly cool.
records.story: Ribeira Sacra was confirmed as a denomination in 1996, a year after its first recognition, its eastern subzone, Quiroga-Bibei, following the Sil and its tributary the Bibei towards Valdeorras. The Bibei valley's walls are steep, and many of its old terraces had fallen out of use when a businessman returning to his family's roots, as his importers tell it, set out to bring them back. The estate was founded at Manzaneda in the early 2000s, in 2000, 2001 or 2002 by different accounts, and its first wines came with the 2002 vintage. The house set about restoring the valley's high terraces, and its range took a family of names: Lalama and Lacima among the reds, Lapena and Lapola among the whites, and Lalume, a Treixadura led white of the Ribeiro denomination. Lalama, the red led by Mencía, kept the valley's old native grapes in the blend beside it, and merchants count the house among the pioneers of Ribeira Sacra's modern wines. For a sommelier Lalama shows the denomination's eastern face, by the Valdeorras border: Mencía with its native partners, native yeasts, wooden vats and patience in used wood.

others.name: Lacima
others.note: The house's other Ribeira Sacra red, also led by Mencía.

others.name: Lapola
others.note: A Godello based white of Ribeira Sacra, beside Lapena, the house's other white of the denomination.

others.name: Lalume
others.note: A white of the Ribeiro denomination led by Treixadura, not a wine of Ribeira Sacra.

traps: Lalama, Lacima, Lapola and Lalume are wines of one house: the reds and Lapola are Ribeira Sacra, while Lalume is a Ribeiro white.
Dominio do Bibei is a Ribeira Sacra house, though its valley runs up to Valdeorras; the Val do Bibei printed on a Godello of O Bolo lies inside Valdeorras.

cards.front: Dominio do Bibei: how is Lalama made in the cellar?
cards.back: Fermented with native yeasts in open wooden vats, then raised in used barrels and larger vats.

cards.front: Where does Dominio do Bibei farm, and beside which denomination?
cards.back: The Bibei valley in Quiroga-Bibei, Ribeira Sacra's eastern subzone, on the border with Valdeorras.

questions.q: A guest asks what goes into Dominio do Bibei's Lalama beside Mencía. Which answer fits?
opts: Brancellao, Mouratón and Sousón
A quarter of Tempranillo from Rioja
Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot
Godello pressed with the red skins
questions.exp: Lalama is mostly Mencía with small shares of the valley's native reds, Brancellao, Mouratón and Sousón, and a little Garnacha; it holds no grape of Rioja or Bordeaux.

questions.q: Dominio do Bibei set out to bring back the old terraces of the Bibei valley. With which vintage did its first wines come?
questions.exp: The estate was founded in 2000, 2001 or 2002 by different accounts, and its first wines came with the 2002 vintage; 1932 is the year Ribeiro, not Ribeira Sacra, was protected.

report: Searches for this record: 6 of the group's share of 35, beside the one shared with Algueira on the Consejo's domain; one on the house's own domain found nothing, so the record rests on the Consejo's page and on importers' and merchants' pages read through search.

Founded is empty: the estate is founded in 2001 in most accounts and conceived or founded in 2000 in others, and Spanish Wine Lover has the family buying land at Manzaneda from 1995; the first wines of 2002 rest on Spanish Wine Lover and a Gourmet Hunters listing.

The plan's note is answered: the label is Lalama, Ribeira Sacra, on Liberty Wines and Skurnik; the grapes are Mencía at about 85 to 90 per cent by vintage with Brancellao, Mouratón, Sousón and Garnacha (Wine.com's 2012, the 2006 note), while Skurnik writes Garnacha Tintorera, so the checker should settle which Garnacha.

Lacima is a Ribeira Sacra red on two merchants' pages and the house's reds are Mencía led by Spanish Wine Lover; the house's other white is Lapola, not Lapena as the plan's note has it, and Lalume is a Ribeiro white by Liberty and Skurnik.

The making: destemmed, native yeasts and large open wooden vats for the 2017 (Skurnik's note), older Burgundy casks (an importer's page), 21 months on the lees in 500 litre barrels for the 2006 and 12 months in 300 litre barrels and foudres for the 2022, hence a year to nearly two by vintage.

Left out for want of a second source: Roman terraces and the valley's emptying by phylloxera and emigration (one importer), the house's consultants from Priorat until 2015 (one listing), its biodynamic farming and every figure of size; the heights are 200 to 700 metres in one account and 350 to 920 in another, hence a few hundred metres to above 700.
Living names met, none in the fragment's prose: the founder, his brother the fashion designer, the two Priorat consultants and the house's first winemaker, all said by role or left out.

wine.name: Viña Costeira
wine.grapes: A blend led by Treixadura, with Torrontés, Godello, Albariño and Loureira in smaller shares that change from year to year.
wine.sites: Members' vineyards on the slopes of the Miño and Avia valleys around Ribadavia, on soils mostly of weathered granite.
wine.making: The grapes of each variety are fermented apart at low temperature in stainless steel tanks and blended afterwards; the wine sees no oak and is bottled young to keep its freshness.
wine.glass: Lime blossom and fresh grass over ripe, faintly exotic fruit; light, dry and crisp, rounder than a coastal Albariño, with a clean, gently savoury finish.
wine.ageing: Made to drink young, within a year or two of the vintage, while its blossom and freshness last.
wine.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, as for a light white; no need to decant; a white wine glass.

label.means: The denomination of the Miño, Avia and Arnoia valleys around Ribadavia, protected in 1932.
The trading name of Vitivinícola del Ribeiro, the growers' co-operative of Ribadavia founded in 1968.

records.table: Viña Costeira is the white of Ribeiro's growers' co-operative at Ribadavia, founded in 1968: a blend led by Treixadura with other native grapes, made without oak and bottled young. Light, crisp and scented with lime blossom, it is a Ribeiro to pour young beside seafood or empanada.
records.story: Ribadavia, where the Avia meets the Miño, was long the trading heart of Ribeiro's wine, which by the denomination's own account reached the rest of Europe with merchants on the road to Santiago, the English becoming its main buyers abroad in later centuries. The town's ordinances of 1579 already fixed the parishes where Ribeiro could be made and sold, and the denomination was protected in 1932, its regulating council formed on 6 December 1956. In 1968 the growers of the district joined in a co-operative, Vitivinícola del Ribeiro, to make and sell their wine together, and Viña Costeira became its name on the shelf. Its members later went back to Treixadura and the district's other native white grapes, and the co-operative is described as a pioneer of the native varieties' return. It makes wines of both Ribeiro and Valdeorras, from this everyday blend to the Treixadura led Colección 68 and a sparkling wine. For a sommelier Viña Costeira is a Ribeiro a guest is likely to have met: a co-operative's blend of native grapes under a wine name that Ribadavia's ordinances guarded as early as 1579.

others.name: Viña Costeira Colección 68
others.note: The co-operative's premium Ribeiro white, mostly Treixadura with small shares of Albariño and Godello.

traps: Viña Costeira is a co-operative's brand, not a single estate: the wine is a blend from many members' vineyards.
Ribeiro's Torrontés is a Galician white grape, a different variety from the Torrontés of Argentina, which springs from Muscat of Alexandria.
Ribeiro is not Ribeira Sacra: Ribeiro is the white wine country around Ribadavia, Ribeira Sacra the Mencía canyons of the Sil and the Miño.

report: Searches for this record: 8 of the group's share of 35 (two on the co-operative's own domain, one on the DO Ribeiro's), and the co-operative's own pages gave little beyond its range and its two denominations.

The plan's note is answered: the co-operative is Vitivinícola del Ribeiro S.C.G., at Valdepereira in Ribadavia, founded in 1968 by Vinetur, Winedering and Enprimeurclub; that Colección 68 is named for the year is not borne out by any page read and is left out.

The blend differs by listing: Ultracomida gives Godello, Treixadura, Torrontés and Loureira, another merchant adds Albariño, and En Copa de Balón's 2022 has more than six native grapes, hence the record's wording; the fermentation of each variety apart in cool steel rests on En Copa de Balón alone and is hedged, the want of oak on two listings.

The tasting words: lime blossom from an International Wine Challenge note of the Viña Costeira Ribeiro, fresh grass and tropical fruit from a merchant's note; the challenge's green apple, white peach and apricot belong to the co-operative's Treixadura and are kept out.

The 1579 ordinances, the protection of 1932 made law on 26 May 1933, the council of 6 December 1956, the English buyers and Treixadura as the queen of the whites are all on the DO Ribeiro's own pages; the region record's 1932 under the Estatuto del Vino agrees.

Left out for want of a second source: the co-operative's member counts and size, its Finca Adega Vella on the Avia, Lua Jazz Brut as the first sparkling wine of Galicia, and every serving temperature the merchants give; the record follows the Codex's light white.
No living person is named or met in this record.
